name: Your Agent's Errors Return 200
question: Why does your retry logic never fire when the agent is wrong?
problem: The agent's answer is wrong, the status is 200, the JSON is valid, and nothing retries. Checking whether it's true takes another model call, which costs about as much as the answer.
points: Ration "is this true?" checks. Each one is another model call.
Check that every id and number in the output came from the input. It's a string operation, and it catches invention.
Spend the second model call only where the action can't be undone.
title: Your AI Agent's Errors Return 200 — Why Retry Logic Never Fires #shorts
cover_title_alt: TRUTH IS EXPENSIVE. PROVENANCE IS CHEAP.
caption:
so... your agent returned a wrong answer. But.. the status is 200. the json is valid. And the retry logic never triggered.

This is the part of AI agent error handling nobody warns you about: an LLM hallucination arrives as a success. Right status, right shape, wrong content. Nothing throws, so nothing retries — and your backoff, your circuit breaker, your dead-letter queue all sit there doing exactly what you asked, which is nothing.

It doesn't improve away either. A better model hallucinates less often; it doesn't hallucinate more loudly. The failures get rarer, which means they're less likely to surface in testing and more likely to reach production unnoticed. The problem gets quieter, not smaller.

Then the part with no analogue in anything you've built before. Everywhere else, detecting failure is free — the exception costs nothing to receive. In an agent loop, the only thing that knows the answer is wrong is another model call. So the cost of checking is equal to the cost of producing. Checking doubles the bill, on every call you decide to check.

You can't check everything. So stop asking the expensive question:

① "Is this true?" needs another model call. Ration that one.
② "Did every id and number in the output come from the input?" is a string operation. Free — and it's what catches an invented object, an id that was never in the input at all. Nothing else catches that.
③ Schema checks catch shape. Grounding catches invention. Together they cost almost nothing and catch most of what actually breaks.
④ Spend the second model call only where the action is irreversible.

Truth is expensive. Provenance is cheap. Build the cheap one everywhere and buy the expensive one deliberately.

Runnable version is in the open vault — a non-deterministic extraction step, four planted regressions, and a scorer that measures both how often your tests flake and how often they actually catch something. Because a green suite means nothing until you know it can go red.
